title: C# Questions & Answers - Integer Data Types
sourceFile: Integer Data Types - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on various data types in integer in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: How many bytes are used to store a 'long' data type in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, the 'long' keyword is an alias for 'System.Int64', which represents a 64-bit signed integer and occupies 8 bytes.

questions.question: Which .NET class is the C# 'uint' data type derived from?
questions.explanation: C# types are aliases for .NET System classes: short (Int16), uint (UInt32), ulong (UInt64), and ushort (UInt16).

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct declaration and initialization of two integer variables?
questions.explanation: Option A fails because 40.6 is a double. Option B fails because 'b' is not declared. Option D fails if 'b' wasn't previously declared. Option C is the correct standard syntax.

questions.question: What will be the error in the following C# code?

options.text: 'k' should not be declared as a constant
The expression assigned to 'k' must be a constant
'm' is declared in an invalid format

questions.explanation: In C#, a 'const' variable must be initialized with a value that can be fully computed at compile-time. Since 'n' is a regular variable, its value could change, so 'k' cannot be a constant based on 'n'.

questions.question: Arrange the following data types in order of increasing bit-size: sbyte, short, long, int.
questions.explanation: The sizes are: sbyte (8-bit), short (16-bit), int (32-bit), and long (64-bit).

questions.question: Which data type is generally preferred for storing a simple integer like 35 to maximize execution efficiency on most systems?
questions.explanation: The 'int' type is the natural word size for the processor (32-bit). Using smaller types like sbyte or short can sometimes be slower because the CPU often converts them to 32-bit integers during calculations anyway.

questions.question: What is a key difference between Convert.ToInt32() and Int32.Parse() when handling a null string?

options.text: Convert.ToInt32() returns 0 for a null string, while Int32.Parse() throws an exception
Int32.Parse() is more efficient for all data types
There is no difference between the two

questions.explanation: Convert.ToInt32(null) is designed to handle null by returning 0. Int32.Parse(null) will throw an ArgumentNullException.

questions.question: Assuming: int a=12, float b=3.5. What is the correct way to assign the result of (a + b) to an integer variable 'c'?

options.text: Both B and C are valid C# syntax

questions.explanation: Since (a + b) results in a float, you cannot implicitly assign it to 'int c'. You must either cast 'b' to int before adding or use the Convert class to handle the conversion.

questions.question: Which C# code correctly prints 74 given a = 12 and b = 6.2f?

options.text: int a = 12; float b = 6.2f; int c = (int)(a / b + a * b); Console.WriteLine(c);
int a = 12; float b = 6.2f; int c = a / (int)b + a * (int)b; Console.WriteLine(c);
int a = 12; float b = 6.2f; int c = a / Convert.ToInt32(b) + a * Convert.ToInt32(b); Console.WriteLine(c);

questions.explanation: Convert.ToInt32(6.2) rounds to 6. Calculation: 12 / 6 + 12 * 6 = 2 + 72 = 74. Casting (int)b would also work (results in 6), but option C is specifically formatted to reach exactly 74.
Case i: 107 / 19 (integer division) = 5. Case ii: 107 / 19.0 (float division) = 5.63, which Convert.ToInt32 rounds to 6. The outputs are 5 and 6.

questions.question: What is the default type of a whole number literal (without a decimal point) in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, a numeric literal without a suffix and without a decimal point is treated as an 'int' (32-bit signed integer) by default.
